title: bolt jig
description: A bolt configuration file: a set of independent tasks, each a command line and optionally something that reads its output and returns a verdict. Derived from internal/descriptor/descriptor.go rather than from example files, so it describes what the parser accepts rather than what the examples happen to use.

version.description: Configuration format version. Only 1 exists; a file naming any other version is rejected rather than assumed forward-compatible.

timeout.description: Bounds the whole run, distinct from any per-invocation timeout. Tasks the budget did not reach are recorded as failures rather than omitted.

defaults.description: Applied to any task that does not state the field itself, because repeated configuration is configuration that drifts. `command` is deliberately absent: a task must never inherit its most important field silently.

tags.description: Accumulate onto a task's own tags rather than replacing them, since both are true of the task.

definitions.description: Somewhere legal to declare YAML anchors for reuse within this file. bolt provides no second fragment mechanism, and anchors do not cross files -- each configuration is its own YAML document.

tasks.description: Tasks are independent and merge; there is no ordering and no dependency between them. A thing that produces no mergeable verdict is not a task.

runtime.description: Named for what the process receives. `once` is the default because it is the only runtime needing no placeholder -- a task that wants files must say which shape it wants them in.

capture.description: `never` still keeps the exit code, which is never the bulky part. For a per-file task over a large tree this is the difference between a readable artifact set and hundreds of megabytes of stored scrollback.

select.description: Filters the incoming file list to the files this task is about. Meaningless on a `once` task, and declaring one there is an error rather than a line that does nothing. Selecting nothing plans nothing: an empty substitution would turn `ruff check {files}` into `ruff check`, which checks the whole tree.

include.description: Globs in which ** matches zero or more path segments, zero included. An absent include admits everything.

evidence.description: A file the task promises to produce. A run that reports success without producing the file it promised did not measure anything; declaring it turns that from a silent gap into a failure.

path.description: A glob, resolved against the invocation's scratch directory and then the run root.

format.description: The format the file must parse as. Inferred from the extension when unset. An empty file fails every format, including text: a tool that created its output and wrote nothing to it did not finish.

required.description: Fails the task when nothing matches path. Set false for a file a tool writes only sometimes, and say why in a comment.

schema.description: Path to a JSON Schema the file must satisfy.

id.description: Becomes part of an artifact filename, so it may not contain a path separator or `..` -- a filename can never escape the artifact directory.

description.description: What the task asserts, in the present tense. Shown by `bolt tasks`.

tags.description: A tag is how a set of tasks gets a name, for --with and --without.

command.description: A shell line. Asks for exactly the substitution its runtime performs: {file} under eachFile, {files} under allFiles, {configdir} and {root} in any. A placeholder the runtime cannot fill is rejected at parse time rather than left unfilled.

requires.description: Executables this task cannot run without. Resolved before anything starts, failing the task once and naming the executable. Undeclared, a missing tool arrives as a shell-level exit 127, indistinguishable from a tool that genuinely exits 127.

timeout.description: Bounds this invocation, defaulting to 120s. A wedged checker does not wedge the run.

tty.description: Allocate a pseudo-terminal. A terminal is one channel, so stdout and stderr arrive merged and cannot be told apart afterwards -- recorded in the envelope rather than left to be inferred from an empty stderr.

result_command.description: Turns this task's execution record into a verdict. A command-line contract, so it may be written in any language: the record arrives on stdin as YAML, {record} is replaced by a path to the same record, and an envelope is returned on stdout. Absent, exiting 0 is the task's whole contract.

output.description: Files this task promises to write.

allOf.description: A filter is meaningless on a task that receives no files, and declaring one is an error rather than a line that does nothing.
Runtime `once` is the default, so a task with no runtime and a select is the same error.
